messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: possible cross-customer prefix bleed detected in dedicated pool gpu-pool-9. Alert triggered by HelixCare reporting other-tenant request ids appearing in their debug logs. Investigating. Thread root ts=2240001111

sre_alex: I'm on it. Picking up pager. Can someone confirm whether this is KV-cache or proxy prefixing? First priority: contain.

maria_runtime: quick check — I can run a scan for inconsistent prefixes in the pool's kv caches. If it's cache prefix normalization that's the culprit, we should isolate pool and stop routing new HelixCare traffic there.

devin_eng: running quick checks now. Sharing commands I'm using:

```
# list nodes in pool
rctl nodes --pool gpu-pool-9 --short
# scan Redis namespace 3 (kv cache shard) for HelixCare prefix
redis-cli -h redis-gp9 -n 3 --scan --pattern "hc:*" | head -n 100
# grep for other-tenant prefixes mapped into hc namespace
redis-cli -h redis-gp9 -n 3 --scan --pattern "*" | grep -E "atlas:|azura:|othercust:" | wc -l
```

devin_eng: got preliminary numbers — 7 keys that look like atlas: prefixed entries present under the same node's view. Not yet sure if that's read-only residual or actively serving.

emily_cs: HelixCare (customer) is asking for immediate status. Do we know if PII may have been exposed? Need count of affected requests before we update them.

sre_alex: @devin_eng prioritize traces for the 7 request ids. Pull the last 1k lines of access logs from node-9-7 and filter for those ids. If we confirm cross-tenant tokens were served, we escalate to privacy. Also set pool to maintenance mode to stop new sessions.

maria_runtime: maintenance mode command: `rctl pool set-maintenance gpu-pool-9 true` — I'll run it. Doing now.

ops_bot: Deploy bot: triggered maintenance flag change for pool gpu-pool-9 by maria_runtime at ts=2240001185.

devin_eng: logs snippet (redacted):
```
[2026-03-14T08:19:12Z] node-9-7 req=hc-req-21 response=... payload-snippet="...atlas:resp-id-442..."
[2026-03-14T08:19:13Z] node-9-7 req=atlas-req-442 response=... payload-snippet="...hc:meta..."
```
This looks like observed interleaving. Could be proxy prefix normalization where prefixes are stripped then reattached incorrectly.

emily_cs: Dev, can you quantify how many unique HelixCare requests contain snippets referencing atlas ids? We need a customer-facing impact statement.

devin_eng: running a grep over last 48h — preliminary: 11 HelixCare request ids with artifacts referencing atlas ids, 3 of those likely included small debug fields (no full docs). I'm still pulling full request/response bodies for those 3.

privacy_oncall: Please preserve all logs and evidence. If there's potential cross-tenant data exposure we need a full chain-of-custody. Do NOT purge anything. Collect network captures for node-9-7 and metadata for relevant redis shards. I'll open a ticket.

sre_alex: Action plan (short):
- contain: pool in maintenance (done)
- isolate: evict node-9-7 from serving and cordon it (I will run eviction)
- audit: run KV prefix audit and access-log correlation (devin + maria)
- mitigate: route HelixCare to fallback dedicated pool (maria ops)
- notify: prepare interim customer message (emily)
- privacy: evidence collection and formal review (privacy_oncall)
Assigning owners: eviction=alex, audit=devin+maria, routing=alex+maria, customer comms=emily, privacy=privacy_oncall.

maria_runtime: evict command: `rctl node evict node-9-7 --pool gpu-pool-9 --reason "suspected prefix bleed"` — I'll run after I snapshot Redis keys. Snapshot saved to s3://incidents/2240001111/kvsnap-9-7.tar.gz

ops_bot: node-9-7 eviction started by maria_runtime at ts=2240001250 — job id j-9812.

devin_eng: audit results summary: found normalized prefix codepath in proxy v2.3.1 that strips everything up to first colon and reattaches using requesting tenant's prefix when cache miss occurs. Repro: yes on staging. I have a dev patch that forces canonical prefix attach. Pushing patch to canary now.

ops_bot: ci/cd: canary deployment started for canary/proxy-fix v0.2.3-canary at ts=2240001320.

emily_cs: Draft for HelixCare interim: "We've detected unusual debug identifiers in logs and have taken your traffic out of the affected pool while we investigate. Our initial analysis shows a small number of request artifacts referencing other tenant ids; we are preserving all data and will update within 4 hours with scope and remediation. — Emily, Customer Ops" Any updates I should include?

privacy_oncall: That message is fine but add that we've initiated a privacy review and are preserving all logs; offer to set up a call if they want immediate handoff. Also collect the 11 request ids for formal incident record.

sre_alex: Can we quantify percentage of HelixCare traffic affected? Devin?

devin_eng: rough estimate <0.02% of requests hitting that node in the 48h window. Noting that HelixCare had uneven load concentrated during their late-night batch.

maria_runtime: mitigation complete: pool maintenance active, node-9-7 evicted, HelixCare routed to gpu-pool-11 (fallback). Routing rule applied: `route override helixcare -> gpu-pool-11 until 2026-03-15T12:00Z`

ops_bot: route-change: override applied by maria_runtime at ts=2240001375.

devin_eng: canary patch shows no cross-prefix reattach on staging. Waiting for canary health metrics (5m). If green, we'll roll to prod but only for proxy instances servicing dedicated pools.

privacy_oncall: copying internal privacy checklist: evidence saved to incident ticket IN-2240001111, IBR preserved, request ids documented. Next step: formal scope determination and notification plan if exposure confirmed.

emily_cs: Sending interim message to HelixCare now and offering a call.

sre_alex: Next actions: once canary healthy, roll patch to prod proxy fleet (controlled), re-run full audit across all dedicated pools, then lift maintenance and gradually reroute. Keep privacy and CS in loop. I'll own coordinating the rollout.

oncall-bot: Pager update: incident state -> mitigation in progress, owner=sre_alex, incident_id=IN-2240001111. Last ts=2240001480

maria_runtime: logging final note here — keep this thread open while we complete postmortem. I'll collect the audit outputs and drop into the ticket.

privacy_oncall: I'll prepare the initial privacy report draft and attach the preserved artifacts.

emily_cs: Notifying HelixCare: "We've isolated your traffic, preserved data, and are actively mitigating. We'll follow up with a detailed impact report within 4 hours."

sre_alex: thanks all — I'll update when patch rollout begins.
